## Evidence

Source reviewed at current GitHub main `8450187fb83a2cb236dfd5d61ec2deb20b910ade` (1 October 2026). The local checkout is older; changed migration files were inspected directly from this fetched commit. These are source observations and proposals, not claims of measured production incidents or performance.

- [src/lib/content/drafts.ts](https://github.com/Reedtrullz/Frontpage/blob/8450187fb83a2cb236dfd5d61ec2deb20b910ade/src/lib/content/drafts.ts)
- [src/components/admin/ProjectEditor.tsx](https://github.com/Reedtrullz/Frontpage/blob/8450187fb83a2cb236dfd5d61ec2deb20b910ade/src/components/admin/ProjectEditor.tsx)
- [src/app/api/data/projects/route.ts](https://github.com/Reedtrullz/Frontpage/blob/8450187fb83a2cb236dfd5d61ec2deb20b910ade/src/app/api/data/projects/route.ts)
- [src/lib/content/publication.ts](https://github.com/Reedtrullz/Frontpage/blob/8450187fb83a2cb236dfd5d61ec2deb20b910ade/src/lib/content/publication.ts)

## Problem

Draft saves replace a whole projects array without an expected draft revision. Publication reads a snapshot, awaits GitHub, then clears both draft keys unconditionally. Atomic rename/SQL upsert protects individual writes, not stale-tab or save-during-publish ordering.

## Proposed PR

Add an opaque draft revision and compare-and-swap saves/deletes; publish against an explicit reviewed revision and clear only the revisions actually published. Apply the same behavior to filesystem and Durable Object persistence.

## Scope boundaries

Owner draft consistency only; preserve independent auth checks and non-force Git refs; no collaborative editor or new persistence framework.

## Acceptance target

- [ ] Two tabs saving different projects cannot silently lose either change.
- [ ] A draft saved while GitHub publication is pending survives cleanup.
- [ ] Stale save/discard/publish returns a actionable conflict; deterministic interleaving tests cover both stores.

## Dependencies

None. Can be developed independently.

Implementation requires a separate task. Issue publication does not authorize code changes or deployment.
issues.title: [Proposal] Prevent stale tabs and publication cleanup from overwriting newer drafts

## Problem

updateHead succeeds before receipt persistence and draft cleanup, but all steps share one catch that reports publication failed. A response lost after ref advancement is also ambiguous. This is a source-demonstrated failure path, not an observed incident.

## Proposed PR

Track publication intent/commit identity and distinguish pre-commit failure, ambiguous remote outcome, and committed-with-local-recovery-pending. On retry inspect the exact remote commit/content before deciding whether another write is needed.

## Scope boundaries

Recovery of this two-file publication only; no deployment or force update.

## Acceptance target

- [ ] Inject receipt-write, cleanup, and response-loss failures after successful ref advancement.
- [ ] UI never says GitHub was unchanged when commit advancement is confirmed.
- [ ] Retry reconciles the original commit, preserves newer drafts, and does not duplicate publication.

## Dependencies

- [FP-01: Prevent stale tabs and publication cleanup from overwriting newer drafts](https://github.com/Reedtrullz/Frontpage/issues/26)

## Problem

versionsMatch extracts an unanchored 7–40 hex substring and accepts matching prefixes; equal arbitrary strings also match. This helper gates remote-head conflict checks as well as the deployed receipt indicator.

## Proposed PR

Separate full-SHA write preconditions from display compatibility. Parse only documented VERSION formats, require full identity for advancing main, and reject malformed or ambiguous values.

## Scope boundaries

Identity parsing only; support documented sha-/ci-/pr- prefixes where appropriate without treating a short display hash as write authorization.

## Acceptance target

- [ ] Embedded hex in unrelated text and dev/unknown identities cannot authorize publication.
- [ ] Full unequal SHAs conflict even with shared short prefixes.
- [ ] Existing documented deployment VERSION formats render correctly; shared caller regressions included.

## Dependencies

None. Can be developed independently.

Implementation requires a separate task. Issue publication does not authorize code changes or deployment.

## Problem

fetchMiningV2 casts external JSON, parses numeric strings without finite checks, has no explicit fetch deadline, stamps collected_at at read time and returns age:0. Public /status shows worker name, exact hashrate, uptime and share counts; its headline uses hashrate>0 without freshness.

## Proposed PR

Use bounded fetch and response validation, retain source/cache timestamps, derive fresh/stale/unavailable honestly, and define an explicit minimal public mining projection with owner-only detail where required.

## Scope boundaries

No wallet balances or worker identifiers in new public output; inspect current intended disclosure with owner before changing product policy. No claim of a demonstrated exploit.

## Acceptance target

- [ ] Malformed numeric/nested payloads never produce NaN, invalid dates or render failures.
- [ ] Stale cached activity cannot be labelled current mining; slow pool API cannot indefinitely block status.
- [ ] Anonymous HTML/serialized payload tests enforce the agreed public projection; owner details remain independently gated.

## Dependencies

None. Can be developed independently.

Implementation requires a separate task. Issue publication does not authorize code changes or deployment.

## Problem

Unsaved guard handles beforeunload and anchor clicks but not all programmatic/history navigation; it also asks on external new-tab links that may not leave the editor. Project discard has finally but no catch for rejected fetch.

## Proposed PR

Define guarded navigation cases, preserve edits on browser back/programmatic transitions, avoid unnecessary new-tab prompts, and catch network failures consistently across editor save/discard.

## Scope boundaries

Use native/browser/router behavior where possible; no persistent browser copy of private drafts unless separately approved.

## Acceptance target

- [ ] Back/navigation loss scenarios are covered without silently discarding unsaved text.
- [ ] Opening a non-replacing new tab does not prompt unnecessarily.
- [ ] Offline save/discard leaves form content intact, clears busy state and announces an actionable error.

## Dependencies

None. Can be developed independently.

## Problem

All non-proxy requests are sent to the Durable Object named primary, and metrics reads decompress stored history. This is a concrete shared execution path; no current throughput/latency bottleneck has been measured.

## Proposed PR

Run a bounded realistic public/owner/collector workload against an isolated candidate, measure latency/CPU/error rates and Free-plan budgets. Document headroom; consider moving immutable public work out only if results justify it.

## Scope boundaries

Measurement first; no automatic sharding, paid fallback, production load test or architecture rewrite.

## Acceptance target

- [ ] Baseline reports exact candidate SHA, request mix/concurrency, duration and budget results.
- [ ] Public reads cannot starve a collector/write in tested bounded scenarios without being reported.
- [ ] Keep current design if measured headroom is adequate; any redesign gets its own approval and evidence.
